clue.text: Gag makes difficulty in breathing

explanation.surface: A choking fit is no laughing matter, though the clue pretends a joke caused it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeze is both a clever trick or prank and the whistling sound of laboured breath.

clue.text: Goddess of the Dead takes early biblical serf

parts.note: Hel is the Norse goddess of the underworld
OT, the Old Testament, is the earlier part of the Bible

explanation.surface: A goddess of the underworld claims an ancient servant from scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is a link. A helot was a state serf in ancient Sparta.
explanation.definitionFit: A helot was an unfree labourer of Sparta, a bondsman.

clue.text: Performance getting condemnation in advance

explanation.surface: A stage show is panned before it opens.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the death penalty carried out, for which a condemnation must come first.
explanation.definitionFit: Execution is the carrying out of a task or piece of music, and the putting to death of one already sentenced.

clue.text: Equal to a five-star meal

parts.note: the proverb says that a sufficiency is as good as a feast, so the clue asks for the word for 'sufficient'

explanation.surface: A restaurant review praising food as good as a luxury hotel's.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is '... is as good as a feast'; 'five-star meal' is a modern feast.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says having sufficient is as good as a banquet.

clue.text: Best man to fight for a cause

definitions.text: man to fight for a cause

explanation.surface: The best man at a wedding is pictured as a crusader.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion is the winner who is top of the field, and also someone who takes up and defends a cause.

clue.text: Girl turns somersaults sideways

parts.note: Catherine is a girl's name
wheels are turns, as in wheeling round

explanation.surface: A girl tumbles head over heels to one side.
explanation.walkthrough: A Catherine wheel is a cartwheel, a sideways handspring, as well as a spinning firework.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine wheels is an old term for cartwheels, acrobatic sideways rolls on the hands.

clue.text: Being docile, gets word of approval-clever

parts.note: amen is said to show assent or approval
able means skilful or clever

explanation.surface: An obedient pupil wins praise for being bright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amenable is tractable and willing to be guided.

clue.text: Pledges for wife in break-up

indicators.note: the wife letter goes inside the turned-up break
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: to snap is to break

explanation.surface: Promises made to a wife fall apart in a marriage breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SNAP to PANS, and 'in' puts W inside it. 'for' is a link; 'break-up' only looks like one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawn is an item given as security, a pledge, so pledges are pawns.

clue.text: Upsets about theatrical performances

parts.note: over means about, concerning
a turn is a short act in a variety show

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by what happens on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn is to tip over or upset, a verb in the third person here.

clue.text: A copper fly

explanation.surface: A policeman described as sharp and streetwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebottle is old British slang for a policeman, from the blue uniform, and also the name of a large blowfly.

clue.text: You do it alone, said Ella Wheeler Wilcox

definitions.text: You do it alone, said Ella Wheeler Wilcox

parts.words: You do it alone, said Ella Wheeler Wilcox
parts.note: the American poet wrote 'Laugh, and the world laughs with you; ... and you ... alone', so the clue asks for the missing verb

explanation.surface: A quotation quiz about what the poet said one does on one's own.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Wilcox's poem 'Solitude': laughter is shared by the world, but crying is done by yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: In the poem, crying, unlike laughing, finds no company, so it is the act done by oneself.

clue.text: Flounder, with wobbly legs, around a basket

indicators.note: the jumbled legs letters sit on either side of the basket
something wobbly is unsteady, so the letters of legs totter into a new order

parts.note: a trug is a shallow wooden garden basket, a British gardening word

explanation.surface: Someone flails about, legs unsteady, while circling a basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flounder' reads as the fish but is a verb here; 'wobbly' jumbles the legs to SGLE, which 'around' splits round the basket.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounder is to thrash about clumsily, which is to battle or strain with difficulty.

clue.text: Like places or possessions that do us credit

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
to set something is to put or place it

explanation.surface: A list of the good things we own that reflect well on us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is only a link between the wordplay and the definition; 'places' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are property and resources, listed on the credit side of an account.

clue.text: Jacob's son who tore the veil

indicators.note: the veil is torn apart, so its letters are ripped into a new order

explanation.surface: A biblical query about which of Jacob's sons ripped the Temple veil.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the veil of the Temple torn at the Crucifixion, but 'tore' simply rearranges VEIL.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis this man is the third son born to Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the priestly tribe.

clue.text: Harden about intent to delight

indicators.note: the hardening word goes about the intent word

parts.note: to enure is to harden or accustom
rapt means wholly intent or absorbed

explanation.surface: Toughen up over a plan to please.
explanation.walkthrough: ENURE (also spelt inure) goes about RAPT.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrapture is to fill with great joy or delight.

clue.text: Our Lily's false as false

indicators.note: the letters of the first two words are rendered untrue to their order, so false signals a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Lily is said to be thoroughly two-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'false' is the anagram signal on OUR LILYS; the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illusory is deceptive or unreal, based on an illusion.

clue.text: Select cap — what a sight it makes one!

indicators.note: the letters of the first two words are made into something new

explanation.surface: Choose a hat that will make you a figure of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it makes one' also hints at the phrase 'make a spectacle of oneself'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a striking sight, often a ridiculous one.

clue.text: Youth ? Not when I was a boy

definitions.text: Youth ? Not when I was a boy

parts.words: Youth ? Not when I was a boy
parts.note: the speaker's young years were not the female kind, since he was a boy

explanation.surface: An old man protesting that his youth was not what the questioner thinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy has a boyhood; the female youth is the other one.

clue.text: New boy in a short pair, to attract

parts.note: pr is the usual abbreviation for pair
to entice is to lure or attract

explanation.surface: A new lad turns up in short trousers to win people over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a short pair' suggests short trousers, but it gives PR. PRENTICE is an old short form of apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprentice is a learner newly taken on at a trade, a novice lad.

clue.text: When Juliet was the sun, this was it

definitions.text: When Juliet was the sun, this was it

parts.words: When Juliet was the sun, this was it
parts.note: Romeo says 'It is the ..., and Juliet is the sun', so the clue asks for the point of the compass he names

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare quiz about Romeo's famous balcony speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun rises in that direction, so Romeo calls Juliet's window there.

clue.text: Searches for frolics.

explanation.surface: A security check is treated as fun.
explanation.definitionFit: To frisk is to pat someone down for weapons, and also to skip or caper playfully.

clue.text: Like a corkscrew the Italian rakes brought back

indicators.note: brought back means the whole run of letters is read from the end

parts.note: la is a form of 'the' in Italian
a rip is an old word for a rake, a dissolute man

explanation.surface: Italian rakes come back looking twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rakes' reads as a verb but is the old noun for libertines; 'brought back' turns LARIPS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew winds round in a helix, which describes a coiled shape.

clue.text: Girl has a head start in tearing up the road

indicators.note: the head's start goes into the torn-up road
the road is torn up, so its letters are dug into a new order
the start of head is its first letter

explanation.surface: A girl races off with a head start along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head start' sounds like a race lead but means the first letter; 'tearing up' jumbles the road to RODA and 'in' puts the H inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoda is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Woman's sex-appeal, given time, wins a patrimony

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
'it' is old slang for sex appeal
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A woman's charm, with time, earns her an inheritance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' and 'wins' are links; IT for sex appeal comes from the 1920s 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrimony is what is inherited from one's father or ancestors.

clue.text: Double Dutch for a gift one's better without

explanation.surface: Gibberish offered as an unwanted present.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'Greek gift' is one meant to harm, after the Trojan horse ('beware of Greeks bearing gifts').
explanation.definitionFit: Unintelligible talk is 'all Greek' to a listener, and a treacherous present is called a Greek gift.

clue.text: Law Lord has, nothing in the game

parts.note: Lud, as in 'm'lud', is how a British judge is addressed
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A senior judge holds nothing back in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'in' are links. LUDO is a children's board game played with dice and counters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a board game in which counters race round a track by dice throws.

clue.text: General knowledge, revised in one respect

indicators.note: something revised is altered, so the letters of one respect are reworked

explanation.surface: A quiz book of general knowledge, revised in one particular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; 'revised' rearranges ONE RESPECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something supposedly confidential that everyone already knows is common knowledge.

clue.text: Girl's around and seen in airy porticos

indicators.note: Vera's is split to go around the word and

parts.note: Vera's, a girl's name with the possessive

explanation.surface: A girl and someone else are seen strolling in breezy colonnades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Verandas are roofed open galleries along a house, open-sided like a portico.

clue.text: Steals peaches

explanation.surface: Someone pinches fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To sneak is to creep or pilfer, and also to tell tales; to peach is old slang for informing on someone.
